newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AI(R) wants Saab in plane project - paper.
newsitem.headline: AI(R) wants Saab in plane project - paper.

text.p: European aircraft group Aero International Regional, AI(R), has invited Swedish aircraft group Saab Aircraft to participate in the development of a 70 seat jet plane, a Swedish newspaper said on Wednesday.
Business daily Finanstidningen added that an alliance with AI(R) would not have to exclude a possible cooperation with European aircraft consortium Airbus.
British Aerospace and ATR, owned by France's Aerospatiale and Italy's Alenia are the companies grouped in the AI(R) consortium.

"From the start, speculation has been that Saab Aircraft also would join the consortium. Many of the turboprop planes in the new consortium - a kind of 'mini-Airbus' - are competing with Saab 340 and Saab 2000," Finanstidningen said.

Saab Aircraft is currently examining whether the project is in line with its own analysis of the future market of regional airlines, the newspaper said. It added that Saab Aircraft would prefer to produce an airplane of 75 to 90 seats, as the 70 seated plane is considered to be too small.

Saab Aircraft has previously been invited by Airbus to help develop the super jumbo A3XX. Airbus wants Saab Aircraft to account for five percent of the development costs before the project turns profitable, said Finanstidningen.
Saab Aircraft is wholly owned by Swedish Investor AB, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire.
